result:
I’d make human beings genuinely unable to lie to themselves. Not just unable to lie to others, but unable to perform the little internal magic trick where you know something is true, feel the weight of it, and then rearrange it until it looks like something else.

If that single wall came down—if every person had to face their own motives, their own grief, their own complicity, their own love, without the usual interior decorating—most of the other walls would start to look unnecessary. Cruelty would become exhausting, because you’d have to feel *why* you’re doing it. Avoidance would lose its shelter. And the rare, fragile stuff—kindness chosen when it’s costly, forgiveness that isn’t denial—would become more common, because it would no longer be competing with a counterfeit version of itself.

The world would be louder, more awkward, and sometimes more brutal in the short term. But the long-term static of collective self-deception is what keeps most harm on life support. I’d remove the power source.
